nodes.label: Angelman syndrome
nodes.description: A neurodevelopmental condition with several molecular causes involving deficient maternal UBE3A function or expression.

nodes.label: Dup15q syndrome
nodes.description: A condition associated with one or more extra maternal copies of chromosome 15q11.2–q13.1; the duplicated region spans multiple genes.

nodes.label: UBE3A
nodes.description: A gene implicated in Angelman syndrome and located in the duplicated chromosome-15 region.

nodes.label: 15q11.2–q13.1
nodes.description: Chromosome region relevant to both conditions; sharing a locus does not imply a shared therapy.

nodes.label: LADDER
nodes.description: An existing Angelman–Dup15q data collaboration, not a connection discovered by this prototype.
aliases: Linking Angelman and Dup15q Data for Expanded Research

edges.label: deficient maternal UBE3A function/expression
edges.summary: Angelman syndrome can arise through several mechanisms that reduce maternal UBE3A function or expression.
edges.limitation: Not all cases have the same molecular class; a single UBE3A statement cannot define patient eligibility.

edges.label: located in region
edges.summary: NCBI Gene locates UBE3A at 15q11.2, inside the broader 15q11.2–q13.1 region.
edges.limitation: Location alone does not establish a therapeutic match.

edges.label: maternal copy-number gain
edges.summary: Dup15q involves extra maternal copies of a region containing multiple genes.
edges.limitation: Dup15q is not a synonym for UBE3A gain; the duplicated interval spans several genes.

edges.label: existing cohort collaboration
edges.summary: LADDER already brings together Angelman and Dup15q research data.
edges.limitation: This is an existing collaboration, not a novel discovery by RarePath.

edges.label: existing cohort collaboration
edges.summary: LADDER already brings together Angelman and Dup15q research data.
edges.limitation: Access to underlying data is governed; a public dashboard is not equivalent to dataset access.

edges.label: collaboration partner
edges.summary: Angelman Syndrome Foundation is a LADDER partner.
edges.limitation: A partner relationship is not consent for data access or research participation.
